key_insight: The paper reframes medical agents as sequential decision systems that should scale from assisted to fully autonomous operation through better frameworks, capabilities, and clinical environments.
clinical_relevance: It highlights that trustworthy clinical deployment depends less on model size alone and more on contamination-resistant benchmarks, tool integration, and interactive training in PACS, EHR, and FHIR settings.
method: Defines medical agents as partially observable sequential decision-making systems
Introduces a three-level autonomy taxonomy: assisted, cooperative, autonomous
Organizes the field around framework scaling, capability scaling, and environment scaling
evidence_signal: The abstract synthesizes more than 300 references and emphasizes deployment-oriented evaluation rather than reporting a single new dataset or experiment.
watch_item: Clinical self-evolution and autonomy raise safety risks from hallucinations, cascading failures, and fairness issues if environmental feedback is not tightly controlled.
paper_title: The Path to Self-Evolving Clinical Systems: Scaling Medical Agents from Assistance to Autonomy
